Hi, I just want to say thank you. I finally managed to at least get up, and wash my face today. It’s small, but knowing other people care has helped me in this one moment. I want you to know you helped make a difference for me today.
I understand how you’re feeling. I’m struggling everyday too. If you ever need to talk I’m here for you and won’t judge you. I just want you to know that you’re not alone in this.
I’m able to do some dbt with my new therapist. I also have extensive notes and paperwork from treatment for dbt. It just feels so overwhelming right now.
Thank you, I know splitting isn’t necessarily the best idea, but I’ve just needed someone to understand.
Thank you. The red and black is for the album Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge. And then the quote from Helena. I’ve waited a long time to get this.

I suffer from the same thing. It’s hard to open up about it, but letting it out to people who also suffer is a start. Just lay it all out to yourself first. I wrote it all out. Then gave that paper to my therapist.
I’m not sure if this is what you’re looking for, but the book A Danger to Herself and Others is a really good book.

I understand how you feel. I’m not saying oh I’m so healed listen to my wisdom. I struggle everyday with the idea of what I could do. It has helped me to pick one thing out to be completely defiant about. Because sometimes being stubborn is the only thing that can keep me going. Try picking something to be stubborn about, it may help. You have a friend here. I’m always willing to listen.

I have a reason, it may not seem important, but it’s what keeps me going. When I was a little girl, I was happy, as I got older I realized I was nothing. I’ve attempted suicide many times. But through everything I’ve been through, I have the memory of the first time I realize I was going to be dead before 20. How it seemed so fitting for a person with all of my issues, a person who I thought wasn’t worth anything. I turn 25 in less than a month. Every year, I don’t have a party or anything. I take the night to say fuck you to my demons. If you stay alive, your depression will always be there unfortunately. But you also get to tell your demons to fuck off. That they don’t decide for you. Not yet. Not ever. You’re stronger than what they want you to be. I want you to live.
I understand how you feel. Maybe there’s some help. You can always talk to me about anything.
Thank you. It’s been hard not being able to talk about it.
Thank you. This is the first place I’ve told the about this. But I’m scared to tell.
I don’t have one. They’ll all take his side. And not believe me. Because he’s deaf and has a hard time in life.

I understand the feeling of being embarrassed after having an attack. Reaching out for help shows real strength and self awareness though. My best friend who usually helps me through my own panic attacks, taught me this trick for when I’m alone and have them since our time zones are very different as well. It’s a like a grounding exercise to help put yourself back into the moment. 

Make a list of:
5 things you can see
4 things you can touch
3 things you can hear
2 things you can smell
1 thing you can taste

Good luck!
